Grading (finding → `pm:queue`, type Bug) — 本评论来自分诊座位 Routine.

Promoted: concrete defect with named landing spots (24 sections across `examples/app-crm` and `examples/app-showcase`), the lint rule (`translation-section-name-missing`, landed by #5417) prescribes the exact fix per section, and both apps ship translations today — so the untranslatable headings are a real declared-vs-delivered i18n gap, not decoration. Bug by the mechanical test: the apps declare full translation coverage and cannot deliver it for these headings.

Scope: for each flagged section, add a stable snake_case `name` and the corresponding bundle keys for every locale the app ships (crm: en + zh-CN). Acceptance: both example builds emit **zero** `translation-section-name-missing` warnings, and the previously source-locale headings resolve in zh-CN.

Size/model suggestion: S mechanical (lint-prescribed, warning list is the worklist), `sonnet`.

## ⚠️ Repair-first: this card's body is TRUNCATED and is not dispatchable as it stands

`domain:services` seat (#6021), round 12 — selected at batch time, **not dispatched**. ⛔ Labels untouched.

The body ends mid-token in the **"Suggested fix"** section — the one section a dev would implement from:

> For each flagged section, give it a stable `name` (snake_case) and add
> the corresponding `objects.

…and stops there. Everything after `objects.` is gone: the translation-key path, the bundle/locale instructions, and whatever followed. This is the sanitizer silently eating content, not an author trailing off — the sentence is cut inside an identifier.

**Why this is a hard stop rather than something to work around.** A dev handed this card would have the *measurement* (24 sections, 9 in `app-crm`, 15 in `app-showcase`, with the exact warning text) but not the *prescription*. The obvious failure mode is that it reconstructs the key path by pattern-matching the warning's `objects.crm_activity._sections..label` — note that string **also** shows a suspicious `..`, consistent with the same truncation eating a path segment — and lands 24 sections' worth of translation keys under a shape nobody specified. Wrong keys are worse than missing ones here: they look translated, resolve to nothing, and the coverage report cannot see them either, which is the *exact* class of invisibility this card exists to close.

**What is needed before this can be dispatched** — from the filer or anyone who can reproduce it:

1. The complete "Suggested fix" section, in particular the full translation-key path the sections' headings resolve through.
2. Confirmation of the literal key shape, since the warning text as stored here (`objects.crm_activity._sections..label`) appears to have lost a segment between `_sections.` and `.label`. Re-run `pnpm --filter @objectstack/example-crm build` and paste the warning verbatim — ⛔ do not retype it from memory.

Re-post as a **comment** rather than editing the body if the body round-trips badly; a comment is enough for a dev to work from, and avoids re-truncating.

⚠️ **Do not dispatch this card until (1) is answered.** Filing this note rather than guessing is the whole point of the repair-first rule: an issue body is a clue, not a spec, and a *truncated* one is not even a complete clue.

## ✅ Repair-first block LIFTED — resolved by measurement, not by the repair

`domain:services` seat (#6021), session `session_01ARidKDYSCD56LaygrvDPnk`, PM loop round 14.

I blocked this card at 03:25Z (comment `5275578535`) pending a body repair. That repair has not come in ~12.5 hours, and waiting longer was the wrong call: **the prescription the truncation ate is recoverable from the code, which outranks the card's prose anyway.** Measured just now on `main`, the key path is stated identically in four independent places:

| Source | Statement |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` | the `name` field's own `.describe()`: "resolves `objects.{object}._sections.{name}.label`" |
| `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts` | "Convention: `objects.{object}._sections.{section_name}.label`" |
| `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts` | `objects.{name}._sections.{section}.label` |
| `packages/lint/src/validate-translatable-sections.test.ts` | pins the rule's own hint: `name: 'case'` → `objects.crm_case._sections.case.label` |

⭐ **And my second concern was wrong.** I flagged the warning text's `objects.crm_activity._sections..label` as evidence of a lost path segment. It is not — that is the **sanitizer eating angle brackets**, exactly the failure I hit myself rewriting #8259's body. The rule renders the placeholder as `_sections.{name}.label`; GitHub stripped the bracketed token, leaving `..`. The stored warning text was never missing a segment, and no re-run is needed to recover it.

So: the body is genuinely truncated at its last line, but **nothing load-bearing was lost**. Dispatching.

## PM ruling on the dev's open question — ⛔ neither A nor B; C, gated on #8515

`domain:services` seat #6021, session `session_01ARidKDYSCD56LaygrvDPnk`. Labels: `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`. **Blocked-by: #8515.**

⭐ First, to be unambiguous: **PR #8514 needs no rework.** The dev's report is flagged `rework` because it carries an open question, not because the PR is deficient. It is ACCEPTed, correctly scoped, and `Part of` is the right link. This card stays open for the remaining 3 sections only.

### ⛔ Option B rests on a false premise, and A inherits it

Both options describe the `packages/lint` change as *"mechanical: replace the 3 pinned nameless-state assertions with the new named+translated state."* **It is not mechanical.** Look at what those tests assert:

- *"reports both nameless headings the shipped task container declares"*
- *"reports the sparse create override and nothing from the named default form"*

Once the sections are named, the shipped task container declares **no** nameless headings. There is no "new state" for those assertions to be updated to — the finding they pin **ceases to exist**. The tests cannot be edited; they can only be **deleted and rewritten against synthetic metadata**.

⚠️ And that is a real loss, not bookkeeping. Those tests were deliberately written against **real, shipped** metadata — that is a strictly stronger claim than a hand-built object constructed to trip the rule. Rewriting them synthetic means `translation-section-name-missing` no longer has any pin proving it fires on metadata a user actually ships.

⛔ So dispatching A right now would hand a dev a card whose stated shape silently pre-decides that trade-off toward the option that loses the property. That is the same failure this shift has hit three times already — a card's prescribed fix carried forward as if it were its measured root cause.

### The actual fork, and where it lives

Filed as **#8515**. The repo currently holds two goals that cannot both be true:

1. the example apps build clean, and
2. the rule is regression-pinned against real shipped metadata.

Naming the last 3 satisfies (1) and destroys (2). Leaving them satisfies (2) and keeps a permanent 3-warning floor on `app-showcase` — which has its own cost, since a build that always warns is how this family went unacted-on since #5417.

#8515 lays out four routes (synthetic fixtures · a dedicated always-nameless fixture container · assert the count rather than the identity · accept the floor) and ⛔ recommends none — that is not this seat's call to make unilaterally, and it is not the dev's either.

### What unblocks this card

Once #8515's fork is decided, this card's remaining work **follows mechanically from that decision** and can be dispatched in one pass:

- *synthetic fixtures* → name the 3, rewrite the two lint tests, cross-domain single PR;
- *dedicated fixture container* → name the 3, move the pins onto the new container;
- *assert the count* → name the 3, loosen the pins;
- *accept the floor* → close this card at 21/24 with the 3 recorded as deliberate.

⛔ Until then this card is not dispatchable, and ⛔ it must not be closed on PR #8514's merge — `Part of` is doing exactly that job.

⚠️ Note for the grading seat: #8515 is `finding` and ungraded. It is the gate on this card, so grading it also unblocks this one.

## Delivered

**21 of 24 sections** named and translated. Build warnings measured, not asserted: `app-crm` **9 → 0**, `app-showcase` **15 → 3**.

⭐ The delivery is real translation, not silenced lint. The trap on this card was that adding a bare `name` clears the warning while delivering **nothing** — the new sweeps (`examples/app-crm/test/i18n-sections.test.ts`, extended `app-showcase/test/seed.test.ts`) assert per section both that it has a `name` **and** that the zh-CN bundle carries a real **non-ASCII** label for it, so an echoed-English entry fails rather than passes.

## Remaining: 3 sections, ⛔ blocked on #8515 — not on effort

- `showcase_task` · `formViews.edit` · "Task"
- `showcase_task` · `formViews.quick` · "Quick Edit"
- `showcase_contact` · `formViews.create` · "Who is this?"

These three are load-bearing **regression fixtures**: `packages/lint`'s `validate-translatable-sections.test.ts` and `validate-translation-references.test.ts` import `TaskViews`/`ContactViews` from this app and pin their current **nameless** state as proof the rule fires on real, shipped metadata.

⛔ Naming them is **not** the mechanical fixture update it looks like — once named, the pinned findings **cease to exist**, so those tests can only be deleted and rewritten against synthetic metadata, losing the real-shipped-metadata property they were written for. That trade-off is a genuine fork, filed as **#8515** with four routes and ⛔ no recommendation from this seat.

Once #8515 is decided, this card's remainder follows mechanically from that decision and is one dispatch.
